label: Structure Computation
notes: Open by stating the two-view structure problem: cameras are known, a noisy match is given, find the 3D point. Stress that because measured rays rarely meet, triangulation is an estimator and our job is to choose the estimator whose objective matches the geometry we actually trust.

label: Noisy Rays Are Skew
notes: Walk through the picture of two back-projected rays. With perfect measurements they intersect at the world point; with pixel noise they pass each other and become skew. The common-perpendicular gap is a useful Euclidean diagnostic but not a projective objective worth minimizing.

label: Linear DLT Triangulation
notes: Derive the four homogeneous equations from x cross PX equals zero. Stack them and take the SVD null vector. Emphasize this is fast and a great initializer, but it minimizes an algebraic residual with no direct geometric meaning, so it is only a starting point.

label: Not Projective Invariant
notes: Explain that a good triangulator should commute with projective change of the world frame. DLT and the midpoint method do not, because their residual norm is not invariant. Image-space correction does commute, because it touches only the measured points before triangulating.

label: Geometric Reprojection Error
notes: Define the geometric cost as the sum of squared distances between measured and reprojected points. This is the maximum likelihood objective under isotropic Gaussian image noise, and it is the quantity the optimal method actually minimizes, unlike the algebraic DLT residual.

label: Optimal Triangulation
notes: State the optimal-triangulation idea: the corrected pair must satisfy the epipolar constraint exactly while staying closest to the measurements. Hartley and Sturm parametrize the epipolar pencil by one scalar and reduce the search to the real roots of a degree-six polynomial.

label: The Degree-Six Polynomial
notes: Show how the cost becomes a one-parameter rational function of the pencil parameter. Setting its derivative to zero clears to a degree-six polynomial; evaluate the cost at each real root and the asymptotic value, then keep the global minimum rather than the first local one.

label: Correcting To Epipolar Lines
notes: Interpret the solution geometrically: the corrected points are the closest points on a matched pair of corresponding epipolar lines. After correction the two rays meet exactly, so any triangulator, even plain DLT, returns the optimal point. Contrast with the cheap first-order Sampson step.

label: Covariance Of The Point
notes: Propagate image covariance through the projection Jacobian: the point covariance is sigma squared times the inverse normal matrix. The largest uncertainty axis stretches along the viewing rays, so a low residual does not guarantee a well-localized reconstruction.

label: Small Baseline Degeneracy
notes: Connect uncertainty to geometry: as the angle between rays shrinks the normal matrix becomes ill-conditioned and depth variance blows up. Teach students to monitor ray angle, not baseline length alone, and to flag distant structure seen under a narrow angle.

label: Cheirality And Line Reconstruction
notes: Add two practical checks. Cheirality requires positive depth in both cameras, ruling out reflected solutions a small residual cannot detect. A 3D line is recovered as the intersection of two back-projected planes, which degenerates when the line lies in an epipolar plane.

label: Workflow And Takeaways
notes: Summarize the recommended pipeline: DLT to initialize, optimal image correction or nonlinear refinement to reach the geometric optimum, then cheirality and ray-angle diagnostics before trusting the point. Recap that the objective, not just the residual, defines a sound triangulation method.
